questions.question: What is the name of a thin layer of ice that forms on road surfaces?
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice on the road. You can see the road through it, so it looks like the road is just wet. Be very careful when it is below freezing and the road looks wet.

questions.question: Where should hazardous materials be loaded and unloaded?
questions.explanation: Heat makes many hazardous materials more dangerous. Always load and unload hazardous materials away from heat sources.

questions.question: In what type of tank is front-to-back surge usually very strong?
questions.explanation: Unbaffled tanks have nothing inside to slow down liquid movement. This causes strong front-to-back liquid surge.

questions.question: Which statement about hot weather driving is true?

options.text: The air pressure in tires will decrease.
The engine oil helps keep the engine cool.

questions.correctAnswerText: The engine oil helps keep the engine cool.
questions.explanation: Engine oil helps prevent overheating. You also need enough water and antifreeze in the cooling system. Antifreeze is important in both hot and cold weather. Note: Air pressure actually increases in heat, so check your tire pressure often in hot weather.

questions.question: How many identical placards must be placed on a vehicle when required?
questions.explanation: Place four identical hazardous materials placards on a vehicle. Put one on the front, one on the back, and one on each side.

questions.question: Why should you check tires regularly in very hot weather?

options.text: Air pressure may increase with the temperature.
The tread wears down extra quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air pressure may increase with the temperature.
questions.explanation: Hot air expands, so tire pressure can reach dangerous levels in hot weather. If this happens, stop and let the tires cool. Do not let air out, as the pressure will drop too low when the tires cool down.

questions.question: The National Response Center must be notified of an incident, except for:
questions.explanation: Report to the National Response Center if there is: death, hospitalization, $50,000 or more in property damage, evacuation of the public, closure of a major route for more than one hour, fire, spillage, or suspected contamination with radiation, bacteria, or toxins. Also report if you think the situation is serious enough to report.

questions.question: When a tire goes flat with a loud bang, when does the truck feel the effect?

options.text: Only if the damaged tire is near the front of the truck.
Only if the truck is hauling a load.

questions.explanation: There is a short delay of a few seconds between when a tire fails and when the truck is affected. Because of this delay, you might think the sound came from another vehicle.

questions.question: When should you check your mirrors?

options.text: When changing lanes, but only when other vehicles are nearby.
When changing lanes, but only if it is dark outside.

questions.explanation: Always check your mirrors for traffic before you change lanes. Make mirror checks part of your regular scanning routine.

questions.question: When turning left where there are two turning lanes, which lane should you use?

options.text: It is better to take the rightmost lane.
It does not matter which lane you use.
It is better to take the leftmost lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is better to take the rightmost lane.
questions.explanation: Use the rightmost turning lane when making a left turn where there are multiple lanes. Large vehicles need to swing right to turn left. By staying in the rightmost lane, other left-turning vehicles will be to your left. This gives you a better view and lowers the risk of a collision.

questions.question: Move over laws require drivers to do what when approaching a stopped emergency vehicle?

options.text: Move to a lane away from the stopped vehicle.
Move to the far side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a lane away from the stopped vehicle.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is stopped on a multilane road, drivers must move away from the lane next to it if they can do so safely. If moving over is not safe, drivers must slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.question: What is true about hydroplaning?

options.text: It rarely happens with large trucks.
It usually happens when driving faster than 65 mph.
It can happen with just a little water on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can happen with just a little water on the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning occurs when a vehicle's tires lose grip on the road and slide on a layer of water. You do not need a lot of water on the road for this to happen.

questions.question: Who must identify the hazard class of materials being shipped?
questions.explanation: The shipper is responsible for identifying the product's ID number, shipping name, hazard class, packing group, and correct packaging, labels, marking, and placards.

questions.question: What should a driver do if given a leaking package or shipment?

options.text: Leave it on the side of the road.

questions.explanation: Drivers must refuse any hazardous materials shipment that contains leaks.

questions.question: What should you do to prevent a trailer from rolling over?

options.text: Speed up when nearing a corner.
Take on-ramps faster than the posted speed limit.

questions.explanation: To reduce rollover risk with a combination vehicle, keep cargo weight as low as possible and drive slowly around turns.

questions.question: When starting a pre-trip inspection, why should you look under the vehicle?

options.text: To see if the vehicle is on an incline.
To check for fresh fluid leaks on the ground.
To see if the vehicle is in a parking spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: To check for fresh fluid leaks on the ground.
questions.explanation: Before inspection, check the vehicle's general condition. Look under it for fresh leaks of oil, grease, or fuel. Check around the vehicle for hazards such as people, other vehicles, or low-hanging wires or branches.

questions.question: When driving a tank vehicle with liquid cargo, what should the driver do?
questions.explanation: When driving a tank of liquid, increase your distance from other vehicles. This reduces the need for sudden stops, which helps prevent the liquid from surging.

questions.question: What should you do if you are unsure if your vehicle will fit under a bridge or sign?
questions.explanation: If you are not sure your vehicle will fit under overhead objects, slow down and take a different route if possible.

questions.question: What is true about eating while driving?

options.text: It is a good way to save time.
It is encouraged during long trips.

questions.explanation: Eating while driving is dangerous because it takes your attention away from the road and requires you to remove a hand from the steering wheel.

questions.question: What is sleep debt?

options.text: When you have not slept enough
When you want to take a nap
The time it takes to get ready to drive after sleeping

questions.correctAnswerText: When you have not slept enough
questions.explanation: Sleep debt builds up when you do not sleep enough. You can only pay back this debt by getting more sleep.
